title: Can the first player always win?
hook: X moves first. Does that decide the game? Score an endgame to see how it's solved.

doesNotKnow: how a game can be solved by working back from the end

misconception: In noughts and crosses the first player, playing perfectly, wins.
objective: The learner can explain that a game is solved by scoring every ending and working upward, with each player picking the best result for themselves (O the worst for X), and that this gives a draw for tic-tac-toe.

claims.text: From the empty board, perfect play by both players ends in a draw.
claims.source: TOLD, NOT SHOWN: the stage scores a 3-empty-square endgame only. Builder's node script (company/reviews/tic-tac-toe-is-a-draw/verify.mjs): memoized minimax (X max, O min, win = +1, draw = 0, loss = -1) from the empty board gives 0; each first move for X (corner, edge, centre) also gives 0. Written without reference to library code.

claims.text: There are 255,168 complete games of tic-tac-toe from the empty board.
claims.source: Builder's node script: exhaustive count of move sequences from the empty board that end in a win or a full board, stopping a game at the first three in a row. Result 255,168. TOLD, NOT SHOWN.

claims.text: From the stage's endgame (X O X / O O . / . X ., X to move), X playing right middle gives O the replies bottom left (then X's forced last move at bottom right wins for X) and bottom right (then X's forced last move at bottom left gives a draw); X playing bottom left gives O the replies right middle (O completes the middle row and wins) and bottom right (then X's forced last move gives a draw); X playing bottom right gives O the replies right middle (O wins) and bottom left (then X's forced last move at right middle wins for X).
claims.source: Builder's node script: all 6 lines played out and scored by the line-completion rule. Scores with O replying best: right middle = draw, bottom left = O wins, bottom right = O wins; X's best = draw. Matches the spec's table (company/design/specs/tic-tac-toe-is-a-draw.md). Demo.tsx computes the same values from the boards.

claims.text: In that endgame X has two moves (right middle and bottom right) with a win underneath, but in each O's best reply takes it away.
claims.source: From c3's script: right middle has an X win after O bottom left but O's reply bottom right gives a draw; bottom right has an X win after O bottom left but O's reply right middle wins for O. O picks the lower of the two in each case. Stage scored values: draw, O wins, O wins.

claims.text: To solve a game, score every ending, then let each player pick the best result for themselves moving upward: O picks the worst result for X, X picks the best.
claims.source: Minimax: von Neumann, Zur Theorie der Gesellschaftsspiele, Mathematische Annalen 100 (1928); Russell and Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach, section 5.2 (page/section numbering not rechecked by the builder).

claims.text: Chess has far too many games to finish this way.
claims.source: Shannon, Programming a computer for playing chess, Philosophical Magazine 41 (1950): about 10^120 possible games as a lower bound. Told in the reveal; builder has not rechecked the figure.

recall.question: X is to move. Scoring each of X's three moves by O's best reply gives: X wins, draw, O wins. What is the value of X's position with perfect play?
recall.why: X picks the move that is best for X, so the position takes the highest of the three scores. Each of those scores already assumed O's best reply.
